articles.title: Indie Hackers Told Me I Was Fixing the Wrong Wall
articles.excerpt: PeerPlay exists because of one rule. I ran into Google Play's closed-testing requirement with my own Android app, needed 12 testers who stayed opted in for 14 days, and could not find them. So I built…
articles.body: PeerPlay exists because of one rule. I ran into Google Play's closed-testing requirement with my own Android app, needed 12 testers who stayed opted in for 14 days, and could not find them. So I built an app where developers test each other's apps in tracked 14-day rounds, with a check that each tester actually opened the app for a real minimum session. Then I wrote about it on Indie Hackers, and the most useful replies were not about the thing I had built. They were about the walls on either side of it. Pushback one: the harder wall comes after day 14 Several readers said the same thing in different words. Passing closed testing gets you into production, and production for a new app means zero ratings and almost no search visibility. The 12-tester rule is a gate with clear instructions.

articles.title: Wholesale and bulk licensing: selling the same download to teams, schools and companies
articles.excerpt: Most digital products are priced for an audience of one: one buyer, one payment, one download. Then an email arrives that does not fit that shape at all. An operations manager wants your template pack…
articles.body: Most digital products are priced for an audience of one: one buyer, one payment, one download. Then an email arrives that does not fit that shape at all. An operations manager wants your template pack for her whole department. A teacher wants your workbook for every student in three year groups. A training company wants to include your course files in the programmes it sells to its own clients. Each of them is offering you more money in a single transaction than a week of single sales — and each of them needs a different price, a different licence and different paperwork than your buy page currently describes. Sellers handle these emails badly in two predictable ways. The first is to quote the single-copy price times the quantity, which usually ends the conversation.

articles.body: This guide was first published on exodus.elim.io . Prices are Google's list prices on the date in the text. Moving from a VPS to Cloud Run puts the app in a container and turns every other piece of the server into a Google service: Postgres into Cloud SQL, uploads into Cloud Storage, crontab into Cloud Scheduler and jobs, nginx into Cloud Run's HTTPS. In our model the bill goes up, from $8.39 to $12.59 a month to $9.59 to $174.52, so move for the work saved. In short On price the VPS wins at every size in our model: $8.39 to $12.59 a month on Hetzner against $9.59 to $174.52 on Cloud Run with Cloud SQL. The systemd unit becomes a Dockerfile; the app listens on PORT, 8080 by default, and finishes within 10 seconds of SIGTERM, where systemd gave 90.

articles.title: The patterns that break on Cloud Run, and their replacements
articles.excerpt: This guide was first published on exodus.elim.io. Prices are Google's list prices on the date in the text. Six patterns break on Cloud Run: a worker waiting on a queue, work after the response, timers…
articles.body: This guide was first published on exodus.elim.io . Prices are Google's list prices on the date in the text. Six patterns break on Cloud Run: a worker waiting on a queue, work after the response, timers inside the app, files on local disk, sessions in memory and long-lived connections. Each assumes a process that runs on its own, owns a disk and keeps its memory. Their replacements are Cloud Tasks, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Storage, signed cookies, and sockets that reconnect. In short With request-based billing, an instance has CPU only while a request is open, and an idle one is stopped within 15 minutes with SIGTERM and 10 seconds.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.title: 'We basically did Top Gun in space': 'Star Trek Starfleet Academy' warps back into action in March 2027 for sophomore year in the final frontier
articles.excerpt: The sophomore season of "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy" will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.
